title: PRISM: LLM-Guided Semantic Clustering for High-Precision Topics
problem: Embedding-based topic models lack local precision to separate closely related narratives within one domain; calling LLMs at inference time is costly.
architecture: Teacher-student distillation: an LLM labels sampled text pairs (binary 'same thing?' judgements in a range-bound similarity window, or teacher-embedding similarities); all-mpnet-base-v2 is fine-tuned with CoSENT loss; thresholded community-detection clustering (items may stay unassigned), threshold tuned on LLM-labelled validation pairs.

datasets.name: HumAID
datasets.details: disaster tweets from 19 events; train 28,802 / test 8,157 after processing

metrics: AUPC (area under the purity Pareto curve)
key_results: AUPC with Emb.&RB fine-tuning: HU .807, IM .966 vs Top2Vec (mpnet) .717 and .913 and teacher-embedding clustering .786 and .957.
On LIAR all methods are close (PRISM .638-.641 vs teacher-embedding clustering .639).
Each LLM-labelled training set costs about $0.20 (comparison) or $0.05 (embedding).
strengths: Cheap: a small number of LLM queries, then a locally deployable encoder.
Allows unassigned items, avoiding forced low-quality topic assignments.

limitations.text: Evaluated with label purity only; topic coherence/diversity are deliberately not used.
Gains on LIAR are within about 0.005 AUPC of baselines.
